macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street rebounded, led by tech and semiconductors
items.summary: U.S. equities finished higher, with the Nasdaq 100 up 1.6% and semiconductors rising about 5% as AI-related names recovered. The S&P 500 also gained, while European markets were slightly softer by the close.

items.title: Major U.S. and global index moves were mixed
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.77% and the Nasdaq 100 advanced 1.62%, while the DAX gained 0.89%; the MSCI world index slipped 0.3% as investors weighed geopolitical and rate risks.

items.title: Fed oversight and policy debate stayed in focus
items.summary: News highlighted new expert groups for a review of the Federal Reserve, while Fed Governor Waller defended forward guidance but called for more flexibility in rate-setting. The commentary added to attention on how the Fed may communicate policy next.

items.title: Central bank expectations in Japan pointed to more tightening
items.summary: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said the BOJ may need more rate hikes if inflation risks remain above 2%, with the timing dependent in part on the impact of the Iran conflict. That kept global bond and currency markets sensitive to policy shifts.

items.title: Oil fell while gold and bonds reacted to geopolitical stress
items.summary: Brent and WTI both declined sharply as markets assessed Middle East tensions, even as gold rose more than 1% and U.S. Treasuries bounced after earlier selling. The moves reflected shifting risk sentiment across commodities and fixed income.

items.title: Dollar steadied as the yen stayed near multi-decade lows
items.summary: The dollar stabilized while the yen remained near a nearly 40-year low, underscoring the pressure from yield differentials and policy expectations. Currency moves were also influenced by labor-market data and geopolitical headlines.

items.title: Tech and AI remained the dominant stock-market theme
items.summary: Market coverage emphasized that Wall Street was advancing on renewed AI enthusiasm, with semiconductor stocks rebounding strongly ahead of early earnings reports. Meta was also reported to plan AI chip production starting in September to expand computing capacity.

items.title: Company and corporate news included Meta, Bank of America, Airbus, and Volkswagen
items.summary: Reported developments included Meta’s planned start of AI chip production in September, Bank of America’s plan to redeem $2.6 billion in senior notes, Airbus labor strikes in Spain, and a VW supervisory board meeting that ended without progress on restructuring plans.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades near $63,057 as crypto market softens
items.summary: Bitcoin was around $63,057, down 0.44% over 24 hours, while Ethereum held near $1,862 and total crypto market capitalization stood at $2.17 trillion. The Fear & Greed Index remained in “fear” territory at 34, and liquidations fell sharply to about $95.9 million.

items.title: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and Solana all edge higher after weekend risk appetite improves
items.summary: Major cryptocurrencies posted modest gains, with Bitcoin at $63,197.96, Ethereum at $1,870.96, XRP at $1.07, and Solana at $73.08. The global crypto market cap held near $2.17 trillion, while trading volume rose and volatility stayed elevated.

items.title: Bitcoin whales push BTC to $64K as Coinbase Premium turns positive
items.summary: On-chain data showed whale demand helping Bitcoin reach $64,000, with the Coinbase Premium breaking a key threshold. The move was framed as a sign of improving U.S. buying pressure.

items.title: Paul Grewal exits Coinbase legal leadership before key CLARITY vote
items.summary: Coinbase’s top legal executive stepped down ahead of a crucial vote on the CLARITY Act, which could shape U.S. crypto-market structure rules. The timing highlights how regulatory uncertainty continues to affect major exchanges.

items.title: Senate debate intensifies over blockchain developer protections in crypto bill
items.summary: Senator Wyden urged Senate leaders to preserve contested protections for blockchain developers in a broader crypto bill. The issue remains central to the regulatory treatment of software developers and protocol contributors.

items.title: European Commission reportedly eyes broader MiCA rules for tokenization and non-EU stablecoin issuers
items.summary: A report said the European Commission is considering expanding MiCA coverage to include tokenization and stablecoin issuers outside the EU. If adopted, the move would widen Europe’s crypto rulebook substantially.

items.title: Hong Kong SFC orders crypto platforms to drop SMS authentication
items.summary: Hong Kong’s securities regulator moved to force crypto platforms away from SMS-based authentication, citing security concerns. The change is part of a broader tightening of operational standards for exchanges.

items.title: XRP rises as SWIFT taps Ripple-linked banks for blockchain payments
items.summary: XRP gained after reports that SWIFT is working with Ripple-linked banks on blockchain payment initiatives. The development added to optimism around institutional blockchain settlement use cases.

items.title: Bitdeer unveils $36 million Nevada factory to expand Bitcoin mining
items.summary: Bitdeer announced a $36 million Nevada factory aimed at scaling Bitcoin mining infrastructure. The project signals continued investment in U.S.-based mining capacity despite a challenging market.

items.title: PayPal brings PYUSD stablecoin to Polygon’s Open Money Stack
items.summary: PayPal expanded its PYUSD stablecoin integration to Polygon’s Open Money Stack, deepening its blockchain payments footprint. The move is notable for stablecoin adoption in consumer-fintech infrastructure.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work and GPT-Live voice models
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent for executing tasks across apps and files, and also launched GPT-Live, a new family of real-time voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.1 with developer preview
items.summary: Meta opened developer access to Muse Spark 1.1, an upgraded AI model positioned as a more capable option for coding and other business use cases.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI rolled out Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and emphasizing improvements for coding and agentic workflows.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body intended to keep the company aligned with its public mission.

items.title: New York Times-led group seeks sanctions against OpenAI in copyright case
items.summary: A coalition of newspapers including the New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI, accusing it of misrepresenting its ability to search systems for evidence in the copyright dispute.

items.title: Meta announces major data center build in Alberta
items.summary: Meta said it will build a large data center in central Alberta, expanding infrastructure to support AI compute demand and its broader AI plans.

items.title: Ollama raises $65 million Series B
items.summary: Ollama, a tool that helps developers run open-weight AI models locally, raised a $65 million Series B led by Theory Ventures.

items.title: Cognition releases SWE-1.7
items.summary: Cognition launched SWE-1.7, a new model trained from Kimi K2.7 and available in Devin at high throughput, with the company claiming it approaches frontier-level performance at lower cost.

items.title: OpenAI broadens release of GPT-5.6
items.summary: Reports say OpenAI has broadly released GPT-5.6 and is pairing it with ChatGPT Work, signaling continued rapid expansion of its model lineup and workplace automation offerings.

items.title: Wimbledon expands IBM AI coverage tools
items.summary: Wimbledon is adding IBM-built AI features to its app and website for live match updates, contextual explanations, and other coverage enhancements, reflecting continued adoption of AI in sports media.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Meta plans first Canada data center and in-house chip manufacturing ramp
items.summary: Meta said it will build its first data center in Canada, a 1GW facility in Alberta expected to cost about $9 billion and take two to three years to construct. TechMeme also reported that Meta plans to start manufacturing its in-house Iris chip from September as part of a broader computing expansion.

items.title: EU court rejects Apple challenge to App Store gatekeeper designation
items.summary: The EU General Court dismissed Apple’s legal challenge to its designation as a Digital Markets Act gatekeeper for the App Store and iOS. The ruling leaves Apple subject to the EU’s platform rules after a case it filed in 2024.

items.title: Block settles Cash App fraud claims for $45 million
items.summary: Block agreed to pay $45 million and provide live customer support for Cash App to settle claims brought by 46 U.S. states. The case centered on allegations that the company failed to adequately protect users from fraud.

items.title: India removes some import duties on phone parts
items.summary: India scrapped import duties on certain components used to make devices such as phones until March 31, 2029. The move removes 7.5% and 5% levies and could benefit manufacturers including Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: SAP avoids EU antitrust fine with contract-switching changes
items.summary: SAP will make it easier for customers to switch to rival providers or end contracts, a move that appears to avert a possible EU antitrust fine. The change follows a September 2025 probe by EU regulators.

items.title: European startup funding jumps to four-year high
items.summary: European startups raised $24 billion in Q2, up 66% year over year and the strongest quarter in four years. TechMeme reported that UK startups led the region with $10.4 billion, ahead of Germany and France.

items.title: South Korea announces massive chipmaking hub investment
items.summary: AP reported that Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plan to invest a combined $518 billion in a new chipmaking hub. The project is intended to meet soaring demand for semiconductors tied to the broader tech boom.
